1	# Building on Windows
2
3	Many of the build scripts are bash scripts and not natively invocable in Windows. To solve this, you can build the project using Git Bash.
4
5	1. Install [Git & Git Bash for Windows](https://git-scm.com/downloads).
6	2. Ensure you have activated [Developer Mode](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/get-started/enable-your-device-for-development).
7	3. Install Node v22.x or greater.
8	4. Clone this repo.
9	5. Using Git Bash (run as administrator), change to the root of this repo.
10	6. From inside the bash shell, run `yarn install`.
11	7. From still inside the shell, run `yarn start:browser`.
12	8. Open your browser to [http://localhost:3001](http://localhost:3001).
13
14	## How to Build the Electron App on Windows
15
16	1. Follow steps 1 - 6 above.

18	3. If you get an error from electron, run `yarn rebuild-electron` and rerun `yarn start`.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-03 23:29:23Z)**_

The build output is now populated (it wasn't before). This confirms what's going on.

## Why you're seeing this

The "critical backend worker" is loot-core's SQLite backend, which runs in a `SharedWorker`. In dev mode it's served from `packages/loot-core/lib-dist/browser/kcab.worker.dev.js`, and that file is **not built ahead of time** — it's built by a background process that `packages/desktop-client/vite.config.mts` spawns automatically the moment the frontend dev server starts ([vite.config.mts:157-172](packages/desktop-client/vite.config.mts#L157-L172)).

On your machine, that directory was empty/missing, so requests to `/kcab/kcab.worker.dev.js` 404'd. The browser worker retries importing that script a few times over ~10-25 seconds ([browser-server.js:12-38](packages/desktop-client/src/browser-server.js#L12-L38)) and then gives up with `BackendInitFailure`, which is exactly the "critical backend worker" message you saw.

I ran the loot-core build manually and it succeeded cleanly in ~3 seconds with no errors, so the build itself isn't broken — the auto-spawned watcher just wasn't producing output for you.

## Most likely explanations

1. **Timing** — you opened the browser before the background build (spawned only when the Vite dev server starts) finished its first pass. This is most likely if `yarn start` was still printing early output when you loaded the page.
2. **The child process silently failed to spawn** — the plugin spawns `yarn vite build ...` via `spawn('yarn', [...], { shell: true })`. If that spawn errored, it only logs `loot-core backend failed to spawn: ...` to the **terminal running `yarn start`**, not the browser — worth checking that terminal's output.

## What to do

- Check the terminal where `yarn start` is running for a line like `loot-core backend failed to spawn` or any error from the `vite build --watch` process — that will confirm which of the two it is.
- Just reload the page after waiting ~10-15 seconds post-startup — now that `lib-dist/browser` has real content, it should load.
- If it keeps happening, kill `yarn start`, delete `packages/loot-core/lib-dist` (`rm -rf packages/loot-core/lib-dist`), and restart `yarn start` fresh.

9	function getGlobalObject() {
10	  const obj =
11	    typeof window !== 'undefined'
12	      ? window
13	      : typeof self !== 'undefined'
14	        ? self
15	        : null;
16	  if (!obj) {
17	    throw new Error('Cannot get global object');
18	  }
19	  return obj as unknown as typeof globalThis & {
20	    __globalServerChannel: Window | null;
21	  };
22	}
23

25
26	function coerceError(error) {
27	  if (error.type && error.type === 'APIError') {
28	    return error;
29	  }
30
31	  return { type: 'ServerError', message: error.message, cause: error };
32	}

34	export const init: T.Init = function (serverChn, handlers) {
35	  const serverChannel = serverChn as Window;
36	  getGlobalObject().__globalServerChannel = serverChannel;
37
38	  serverChannel.addEventListener(
39	    'message',
40	    e => {
41	      const data = e.data;
42	      const msg = typeof data === 'string' ? JSON.parse(data) : data;
43
44	      if (msg.type && (msg.type === 'init' || msg.type.startsWith('__'))) {
45	        return;
46	      }
47
48	      if (msg.name === 'client-connected-to-backend') {
49	        // the client is indicating that it is connected to this backend. Stop attempting to connect
50	        logger.info('Backend: Client connected');
51	        clearInterval(reconnectToClientInterval);
52	        return;
53	      }
54
55	      const { id, name, args, undoTag, catchErrors } = msg;
56
57	      if (handlers[name]) {
58	        runHandler(handlers[name], args, { undoTag, name }).then(
59	          result => {
60	            serverChannel.postMessage({
61	              type: 'reply',
62	              id,
63	              result: catchErrors ? { data: result, error: null } : result,
64	              mutated: isMutating(handlers[name]),
65	              undoTag,
66	            });
67	          },
68	          nativeError => {
69	            const error = coerceError(nativeError);
70
71	            if (name.startsWith('api/')) {
72	              // The API is newer and does automatically forward
73	              // errors
74	              serverChannel.postMessage({ type: 'reply', id, error });
75	            } else if (catchErrors) {
76	              serverChannel.postMessage({
77	                type: 'reply',
78	                id,
79	                result: { error, data: null },
80	              });
81	            } else {
82	              serverChannel.postMessage({ type: 'error', id, error });
83	            }
84
85	            // Only report internal errors
86	            if (error.type === 'ServerError') {
87	              captureException(nativeError);
88	            }
89
90	            if (!catchErrors) {
91	              // Notify the frontend that something bad happend
92	              send('server-error');
93	            }
94	          },
95	        );
96	      } else {
97	        logger.error('Unknown server method: ' + name);
98	        captureException(new Error('Unknown server method: ' + name));
99	        const unknownMethodError = APIError('Unknown server method: ' + name);
100
101	        if (catchErrors) {
102	          serverChannel.postMessage({
103	            type: 'reply',
104	            id,
105	            result: { error: unknownMethodError, data: null },
106	          });
107	        } else {
108	          serverChannel.postMessage({
109	            type: 'error',
110	            id,
111	            error: unknownMethodError,
112	          });
113	        }
114	      }
115	    },
116	    false,
117	  );
118
119	  const RECONNECT_INTERVAL_MS = 200;
120	  const MAX_RECONNECT_ATTEMPTS = 500;
121	  let reconnectAttempts = 0;
122
123	  const reconnectToClientInterval = setInterval(() => {
124	    logger.info('Backend: Trying to connect to client');
125	    serverChannel.postMessage({ type: 'connect' });
126	    reconnectAttempts++;

128	      // Failed to connect to client - signal server error

131	    }

This is a different stage: the kcab worker script now loads fine, but the backend (running inside a `SharedWorker`) isn't finishing its own init, so it never sends the `connect` handshake back ([connection/index.ts:152-157](packages/loot-core/src/platform/client/connection/index.ts#L152-L157) waits for that).

**Likely cause: a stale `SharedWorker` from your earlier broken session.** Actual runs the backend through a `SharedWorker` coordinator ([start.ts:50-85](packages/loot-core/src/platform/client/browser-preload/start.ts#L50-L85)) plus a per-tab backend `Worker` loaded via `importScripts('.../kcab.worker.dev.js')` ([browser-server.js:82-95](packages/desktop-client/src/browser-server.js#L82-L95)). Two things make this sticky in dev:

1. **Dev builds have no content hash** (`kcab.worker.dev.js`, not `kcab.worker.<hash>.js`), so a `SharedWorker`/`Worker` process that's already running under that URL survives page reloads and keeps running with whatever it loaded before — a plain reload does not restart it.
2. `browser-server.js` has a `hasInitialized` latch ([browser-server.js:2](packages/desktop-client/src/browser-server.js#L2), [line 61](packages/desktop-client/src/browser-server.js#L61)) — once an `init` message has been processed once, later `init` messages from a reloaded tab are silently ignored.

So it's plausible the worker that's still alive is the one from before the `kcab` build existed (or one that got wedged retrying), and it's just never going to send `connect` no matter how many times you reload the page.

### What to do

1. **Fully close every tab/window pointed at `localhost:3001`** (not just reload) so the browser actually tears down the `SharedWorker`, then reopen a fresh tab.
2. If that doesn't help, force-kill it: open `chrome://inspect/#workers` (or `edge://inspect/#workers`), find the Actual `SharedWorker`, and click **terminate** — then reload the page.
3. While you're there, click **inspect** on that worker instead of terminating — it opens a dedicated DevTools console for the worker, which is where the actual hang/error (e.g. from `sqlite.init()`, `fs.init()`, or IndexedDB) would be logged. The main page console won't show it.
4. Also check DevTools → Application → IndexedDB for the `absurd-sql`/backend database — a blocked/stuck connection there (e.g. an old version still open) would also explain an init that never completes.

Can you check `chrome://inspect/#workers` (or your browser's equivalent) and tell me what shows up there, or what the worker's own console says? That'll tell us definitively whether it's a stale worker vs. a genuine error inside `initApp()`.
